title: S/PDIF (IEC 60958) and HDMI eARC audio receiver: biphase decode, samples to a ring in memory over AXI4
features: spdif_in biphase-mark decode with a UI of UI_CLKS clocks (pulses of 1, 2 or 3 UI); preambles B, M, W.
Locks after 4 good subframes; a bad pulse or preamble drops lock (CODE_ERR_CNT, LOCK_LOST interrupt).
Sample word {chan_b, block_start, V, U, C, parity_err, 2'b00, sample[23:0]} per subframe, DMA'd in 16-word chunks to a ring of RING_WORDS words (a multiple of 16, at least 32).
CS0: channel status bits 0..31 of channel A from the last block (CS interrupt when updated).

fields.desc: chunks lost to a full ring

irqs.name: ERR
irqs.desc: a job ended that saw an AXI error response

sequence: Write CTRL.ui_clks (clock / (128 x fs)), RING_BASE, RING_WORDS, RD_IDX = 0.
Write CTRL.enable = 1 and IRQ_ENABLE with CHUNK.
On CHUNK, read the ring words RD_IDX .. WR_IDX - 1 and write RD_IDX.
notes: m_* is the AXI4 manager port (32-bit address and data, 4-bit ID, no user / QoS); it passes through unchanged. Bursts are INCR, AxSIZE = 2 (4 bytes), 1 to 16 beats, WSTRB = 4'hF, never across a 4 KB boundary; one read and one write burst are outstanding at a time.
spdif_in is the receiver pin (the eARC differential data channel after the PHY). The eARC common-mode channel and ECC are not implemented.
The core testbench prints one `LAT <master> dram R|W <cycles>` line per AXI burst (tb/tv_lat_mon.svh), the regression suite's latency format.
